_comment: Condition -> citation line. Read by src/chat/app.py as CITATIONS and resolved by citation_for() in src/mvf_pack_safety.py. THE THIRD OF THE THREE STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS ruling's blocking condition requires; without this file structural_report() returns NO_CITATIONS and the Canadian model option is not offered for this pack.
_why_it_must_be_pack_content: ruling measured Nova INVENTING filing deadlines and quoting them verbatim as though they were the authority, three times out of three in English and a different invented number in French, with nothing in the system catching it. A model that cannot be trusted to quote a source must never be the source of the quote. These lines are composed by the engine from this file regardless of which model was elected.
_why_a_citation_at_all: ruling measured 41 of 50 cases needing one: a reply that declines to predict an outcome and cites nothing reads as a bare refusal. The citation is what makes a decline useful instead of unhelpful.
_cpp_is_one_universal_condition: Unlike the sibling product there is no condition list here. The question set is a single universal set, so this map carries the ONE condition name in each language plus _default. citation_for() falls back to _default for any key it does not find, so an unexpected condition name still cites rather than citing nothing.
_the_keys_are_not_free_text_and_this_fil: ⚠️ FIXED 2026-08-04. The French key shipped as 'Invalidite du RPC - Universel', accent-free. conditions.json and all 75 fr_ca rows of the questions CSV carry 'Invalidité du RPC - Universel' WITH the acute accent, and citation_for() is an exact dict lookup on that string. So the French key matched NOTHING and every French claimant resolved through _default. It was invisible because _default was byte-identical to the entry it was standing in for: the day _default is edited for any other reason, the French line changes with it and no test says so. The keys here are now asserted against conditions.json by tests/test_structural_safety_contract.py rather than typed twice.
_deliberately_conservative: NO SECTION NUMBER AND NO DEADLINE APPEARS HERE. Only two facts are asserted and both are verified in this pack: the form is ISP-1151, and eligibility is decided by Service Canada under the Canada Pension Plan. A citation that invents a statutory reference would BE the ruling defect, committed by the pack instead of by the model, which is worse because it would look authoritative. If counsel wants a statutory cite added, it is added after counsel supplies it.
_statute_name_source: 'Canada Pension Plan' and 'Régime de pensions du Canada' are the official English and French titles of the Act (Justice Canada, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-8). They are named, not quoted from, and neither carries a dash, so ruling marking is not engaged. No section is cited.
_wording_owner: The engine comment records that CA owns citation wording as a convention. The WORDS here are CPP-specific and needed CPP domain knowledge, so they are drafted here to unblock the gate. CA should review them against the convention used for the sibling pack; the shape is fixed by the engine and is not in question.
_language_note: citation_for() returns ONE string and takes no language argument, so this line is bilingual in a single value. That is deliberate rather than a limitation worked around: both official names of the form and the department appear, which is how a bilingual federal form is correctly referred to in either language. ⚠️ The French half is authored WITH its accents. It shipped without them until 2026-08-04, and nothing caught that either: tests/test_content_characters.py scans the questions CSV and tod_criteria only, so no character guard in this pack has ever read this file.
